topic: Delhi to Agra in *59 minutes*: PM clears
hook: Delhi to Agra in *59 minutes*: PM clears north bullet corridor
hook_b: Could a Taj day trip take under an hour? Minister says *59 min*
tldr: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says PM Modi approved the north bullet train corridor; timings are indicative.

beats.what: PM Modi approved the northern corridor of India's bullet train network, per Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.
beats.why: Vaishnaw announced it in Varanasi on Oct 31, before flagging off the Varanasi–New Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper.
beats.care: No cost, timeline or station-wise timetable yet. The times quoted are indicative, not final.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Oct 31 in Varanasi that PM Modi has approved the north corridor. Indicative times he shared: Delhi–Agra 59 min, Delhi–Kanpur 1 hr 45 min, Delhi–Lucknow 2 hr 12 min, Lucknow–Varanasi 1 hr 21 min, Varanasi–Delhi 3 hr 35 min. The route is planned to run Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Patna, Siliguri and then Guwahati. Cost and completion date: not announced yet. Vaishnaw said it will be fully 'Make in India'.

cards.q: New bullet corridor: what's your condition?
Which city is the planned corridor's far end?
cards.why: Per Vaishnaw, the route extends past Siliguri to Guwahati in Assam.

viz.l: on the planned route, Delhi to Guwahati

insight: The planned line runs Delhi–Agra–Kanpur–Lucknow–Ayodhya–Varanasi–Prayagraj–Patna–Siliguri, then on to Guwahati.

learn.t: A corridor is a planned high-speed line; approval comes before detailed costing and timetables.

watch: Official cost, Cabinet note, and when construction starts.
